rules.title: Cards gate item use
rules.detail: An item may be collected and banked without its card, but it cannot be used or provide a direct benefit until unlocked.

rules.title: Cards gate combat targets
rules.detail: Only attack an NPC when its card is owned. Talking to NPCs is allowed; mandatory quest enemies still require their cards.

rules.title: Uncarded content is free
rules.detail: If an NPC or item has no card in the catalogue, it is fair game. Verify the catalogue before relying on this exception.

rules.title: Cards do not grant items
rules.detail: The account remains Hardcore Ironman: pull the card, then obtain the item through a legal spawn, drop, shop or production chain.

rules.title: Only duplicates are sold
rules.detail: Unique cards remain in the collection. Only duplicate cards may be exchanged for credits.

rules.title: Quest use counts as use
rules.detail: Handing in or otherwise consuming an item during a quest requires its card. Valid substitutes may replace a missing requirement.

rules.title: Foil item families
rules.detail: A foil unlocks every lower-tier item in the same equipment category. A top-tier foil covers the entire slot beneath it; for example, foil Torva full helm unlocks every helmet.

rules.title: Foil boss and pet exceptions
rules.detail: A foil boss unlocks that boss's collection-log uniques. A foil pet unlocks the pet family. A foil quest boss does not unlock every quest ingredient.

rules.title: Harder ruling wins
rules.detail: When a new edge case has no precedent, choose the more difficult reasonable interpretation and record it for consistency.

rules.title: Proportional integrity penalty
rules.detail: If a locked action materially helps progression, repay the advantage with a proportional sacrifice before using the reward.

rules.title: Mystic Cards cosmetic exception
rules.detail: The Mystic Cards cosmetic is whitelisted for Cardcore identity because it offers no gameplay benefit.

principles.title: Unlock whole skills first
principles.detail: Basic tools, gatherers and production inputs create many levels, credits and future acquisition paths.

principles.title: Value obtainable cards
principles.detail: A rare card is dormant without a legal acquisition path. Rank a common tool, rune, NPC or spawn above inaccessible endgame equipment.

principles.title: Prefer multi-benefit grinds
principles.detail: Favor legal activities that combine XP credits, level bonuses, kill credits, useful drops, clues or quest progress.

principles.title: Quest for access and XP
principles.detail: Prioritize quests that open transport, grant large XP rewards, provide quest points or expose an important item source.

principles.title: Bank future value
principles.detail: Keep legal loot and produced-but-locked outputs so a later card can activate an already-stocked supply.

routes.title: Zero-card start
routes.detail: Use safe Agility for initial credits, open packs, then immediately pivot when a card unlocks an entire skill or combat-credit target.

routes.title: Free transport layer
routes.detail: Use home/minigame teleports while coins are locked; prioritize Quetzal and gnome-glider quest access, and use Castle Wars/F2P Ferox routing when useful.

routes.title: Fire Cape build
routes.detail: Seek a legal ranged weapon and ammunition, sustainable food, Prayer training, every Fight Caves monster card, and an obtainable gear set.

routes.title: Community first-hour route
routes.detail: Stop Draynor Agility at 20, take Attack to 8 on Varrock dummies, complete free XP quests, then pivot into Thieving or the highest safe carded combat target.

routes.title: Credit-engine selection
routes.detail: Use fast non-combat XP for steady credits; for combat, farm the highest-combat-level target that is carded, safe and sustainable rather than chasing combat XP alone.
